newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends lower after NY losses.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends lower after NY losses.

text.p: London cocoa futures drifted lower on Monday following losses in New York, but prices held above crucial support levels.

Activity was centred around the Dec/March switch in otherwise thin conditions and spot futures recovered some lost ground. But at the close, the expiring switch stood weaker than midday levels at around 45 stg.
A total of 939 lots were tendered against December on the first tender day which traders said was relatively large.

December ended two stg lower at 867 stg a tonne after rallying up to 888, but larger losses were recorded on other contracts following disappointment by New York's performance after the Thanksgiving break.
The benchmark March contract closed nine lower at 921 with afternoon deals consisting of trade and origin sales.

"Each time this market goes up, it gets knocked down," said one. He added that the technical potential was drying up and the market was more likely to ride on physical news, especially weekly arrivals in Ivory Coast and new crop estimates.
Brokers Merrill Lynch said in their latest bi-weekly commodity outlook that sideways activity was likely to persist.
"We continue to feel the current supply and demand balance gives little reason for the market to do much except drift sideways from here until there is some clearer indications on the crop size.
"For now the production deficit for 1996/97 is still expected to be smaller than the 1995/96 production surplus," it said.

In other news, a selective strike action in the German confectionery industry was disrupting processing schedules. Supplies of chocolate specialities could be threatened if the action intensified but orders for cocoa beans and butter were unaffected.
Technical support on March was pegged at the chart gap between 917 and 914 followed by the recent reaction low of 903 stg.
